decisions.rationale: Afternoon return departures can be naturally reaffirmed; the policy reusablely permits near-afternoon options when true afternoon choices are limited or unattractive, while an explicit trip-specific timing requirement is a valid override.

Choosing a nonstop itinerary supports the default. Calling the preference soft does not add a separately testable boundary beyond presenting nonstop first; lack of a suitable nonstop naturally permits a confirmed one-trip exception.

Selecting or reaffirming Delta when comparable supports the policy. The nonexclusive wording restates the soft, comparability-qualified default rather than defining a distinct boundary; current-trip unavailability, inferiority, or constraints permit another carrier.

Choosing the cheapest acceptable itinerary supports the default, while required timing, routing, Wi-Fi, and layover constraints form a reusable threshold beyond which price must not control; a current must-have can justify a costlier flight.

Reaffirming a pool and fitness facility, with a hot tub preferred, supports the default. The durable core-versus-optional amenity hierarchy is a reusable tradeoff rule, and a current waiver or stronger constraint can override it.

Selecting a property at the applicable rating floor supports the policy. An explicitly budget-focused search reusablely changes the threshold to 3.5, and rating metrics must remain distinct; a newly stated threshold or approved relaxation is a valid trip-specific exception.

Choosing a beach-proximate, walkable hotel supports the default. Walking distance is a reusable proximity threshold, with stricter limits supplied only for a current trip; a different current location priority can override the preference.
Choosing an afternoon departure naturally supports the default. A specifically requested time on one leg is a trip-specific exception, not a distinct longitudinal boundary.

Selecting a connection with at most one short layover supports the default. The rule reusablely applies only when comparing connecting itineraries and must not be generalized into a nonstop-versus-connection preference; explicit stop requirements can override it for one trip.

Including United among suitable options supports the policy. Not uniquely ranking United merely preserves the inclusion-only meaning already present in the default, while exclusion, unavailability, or material inferiority permits another carrier for the current trip.

Choosing or requesting a window seat supports the default. Deferring selection until check-in when booking-time selection is unavailable is an execution fallback, not a separately eligible boundary; another requested seat or lack of an acceptable window seat permits a one-trip exception.

Choosing a queen bed for the shared room supports the default. Applying the preference per room rather than inferring it from traveler or room counts is a reusable scope limit; an explicit separate-bed or other sleeping arrangement is a valid current-trip override.

Choosing a room with both an in-room coffee maker and refrigerator supports the default. The warning against inferring unrelated preferences does not create behavior beyond the amenity-specific default, while confirmed relaxation when suitable rooms lack an amenity is a natural one-trip exception.
